question.text: A company is in default on repayment of deposits accepted from the public. Can it proceed with a buyback of its shares?

answer.text: Yes, if it obtains SEBI approval
No, buyback is prohibited if the company is in default on deposits
Yes, if the default amount is less than 10% of the buyback amount
Yes, if it uses only free reserves for the buyback

explanation.text: The Logic: No company may directly or indirectly purchase its own shares or specified securities if default is made in repayment of deposits, interest thereon, redemption of debentures or preference shares, payment of dividend, or repayment of term loan or interest thereon (NISM-Series-IX workbook, p.221). The Trap: SEBI approval, a partial-default percentage carve-out, or sourcing the buyback from free reserves do not lift the p.221 prohibition. Note: Anchor the prohibition on the p.221 default list rather than on any assumed exemption mechanism.
